claim: R5 source research covers intraday momentum, earnings and filing information, conference calls, news, PIT collection, market-data scope, transaction costs, and paper-execution limitations.
impact_on_spec: Require distinct quant, event, missing-modality, placebo, data, and execution contracts before any forward or paper route.
limitations: A literature and provider review defines testable hypotheses; it does not establish alpha in the local data.

claim: The first half-hour market return from the prior close predicts the last half-hour return; the reported effect is stronger on high-volatility, high-volume, and macro-news days and appears in other active ETFs.
impact_on_spec: Test first-hour continuation separately for midday and last-half-hour holding windows, with volatility, volume, and event-state interactions preregistered as ablations.
limitations: The published evidence uses older high-frequency ETF data; local IEX bars and current costs require independent validation.

claim: Post-earnings-announcement drift is a documented delayed-price-response hypothesis rather than evidence that every earnings surprise remains tradable after modern costs.
impact_on_spec: Treat earnings recency and direction as event-state factors and test them only from timestamped PIT packets against quant-only and event-only baselines.
limitations: Classic historical evidence does not fix a modern horizon, surprise definition, universe, or executable fill model.

claim: Changes in the language and construction of 10-K and 10-Q filings predict future returns, earnings, profitability, news, and bankruptcy outcomes in the reported study.
impact_on_spec: Add filing-change magnitude, risk-language change, and document novelty as forward event factors, with raw source and prior-filing hashes.
limitations: Historical filings need acceptance-time replay and comparable prior documents; the result does not authorize retrospective LLM scoring as pristine OOS evidence.

claim: High media pessimism predicts short-run downward market pressure followed by reversion and unusually high or low pessimism predicts higher trading volume in the reported study.
impact_on_spec: Keep news tone and novelty separate from price continuation and include a reversal control rather than assuming all positive or negative news produces same-direction drift.
limitations: The source studies an aggregate newspaper column, not ticker-level modern API news or LLM-generated scores.

claim: Both earnings-call presentation and analyst discussion segments contain information beyond the press release, with discussion periods relatively more informative in the reported sample.
impact_on_spec: If licensed transcripts become available, separate prepared remarks from Q&A and model guidance change, analyst challenge, and uncertainty rather than one undifferentiated sentiment score.
limitations: The workspace has no registered licensed transcript provider, so transcript candidates remain dependency-skipped.

claim: Managerial positive and negative vocal affect during analyst scrutiny contains information about future fundamentals incremental to quantitative earnings and linguistic content in the reported study.
impact_on_spec: Reserve vocal features as a separate future modality and never infer them from text transcripts.
limitations: Audio rights, speaker diarization, timestamped availability, and a licensed archive are all absent locally.

claim: A recent study reports that larger LLM scores on post-knowledge-cutoff news headlines predict subsequent drift, while strategy returns decline as LLM adoption rises.
impact_on_spec: Use grounded LLM extraction only as a bounded event factor with input and prompt hashes, evidence spans, missing-modality fallback, and forward decay monitoring.
limitations: Working-paper evidence and retrospective model evaluation do not establish local PIT coverage, costs, or independent LLM alpha.

claim: SEC submissions and filing documents expose accession identifiers and filing acceptance metadata suitable for PIT document packets.
impact_on_spec: Bind accession, acceptance time, source URL, fetch time, raw content hash, and prior-document identity before a filing factor becomes visible.
limitations: SEC metadata is not a call transcript; current live collection remains blocked without a compliant contact identity.

claim: Automated SEC access must identify the client and respect the SEC fair-access policy.
impact_on_spec: Fail closed when SEC_USER_AGENT lacks a contact email or URL; never invent an identity in code.
limitations: The policy can change and must be refreshed before operational collection.

claim: Alpha Vantage documents ticker-aware NEWS_SENTIMENT results with topic, publication-time, time-range, sort, and limit parameters.
impact_on_spec: Measure coverage and latency prospectively; provider publication time never replaces collector fetched_at and visible_at.
limitations: The API key is absent, free-tier limits are unmeasured, and historical backfill lacks local first-seen provenance.

claim: GDELT DOC 2.0 supports full-text discovery, JSON output, multilingual search, and a rolling recent-history query window.
impact_on_spec: Use GDELT for forward event discovery and source-diversity measurement, not as a trusted historical sentiment label.
limitations: Entity resolution, duplicates, changing coverage, article rights, and first-seen latency remain unverified.

claim: Alpaca Basic equities data is limited to IEX real-time coverage, while the paid plan provides all-US-exchange coverage.
impact_on_spec: Label the 30-minute cache research-only and require SIP or independent all-exchange comparison before paper readiness.
limitations: IEX-only bars can differ in volume, highs, lows, and opening/closing prints from consolidated data.

claim: Alpaca paper trading omits market impact, information leakage, latency slippage, non-marketable limit queue position, price improvement, fees, and dividends.
impact_on_spec: Paper can validate signal-to-order lifecycle only; matched fills, participation, spread, and adverse selection require separate TCA.
limitations: Real-time quotes do not establish live queue or fill parity.

claim: The amended Rule 605 framework uses detailed order categories, execution timing, effective spread, and realized spread measures for execution-quality reporting.
impact_on_spec: Record decision, arrival, submission, acceptance, fill, and exit times plus implementation shortfall and realized spread by liquidity and time slot.
limitations: This is an execution-quality framework, not a claim that the personal strategy is a reporting entity.

claim: Across anomaly strategies, simple buy-hold spreads and lower turnover materially improve the chance that returns survive transaction costs.
impact_on_spec: Use a small candidate cap, at most one entry and exit cycle per day, and explicit 5/10/20 bps one-way stress.
limitations: Cross-anomaly historical evidence does not substitute for instrument- and time-slot-specific TCA.
